---
title: "Sharpness, detail and size"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Think of printing a road map onto a rectangle of paper. A plot already
fixes the area shown and the size of the rectangle (the panel). Two choices
are left, and each has one place:

- **Sharpness**, how fine the printer is: the device's dpi,
  `ggsave(dpi = 300)`, `png(res = 200)`, or 300 dpi for PDF and SVG. It
  gives more pixels for the same map and changes nothing else: not the zoom,
  not the size of labels, not what is drawn. A basemap's `dpi` is an error in
  a plot.
- **What the map shows**, how big the text and roads are: `zoom` *or*
  `symbol_scale`, in `geom_basemap()` (or `basemap()`, `tm_basemap()`). One
  dial: the area is fixed, so big labels leave room for only the main
  streets, and small labels let many more fit. `zoom` says how much detail;
  `symbol_scale` says how big lines, labels and icons are. Like °F and °C,
  you give one and the other follows; giving both is an error. With neither,
  the symbol scale is 1.

Every picture below is the same 12 km square of Salt Lake City in
OpenFreeMap Liberty, drawn by this code:

```{r}
library(basemapper)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

centre <- st_transform(st_sfc(st_point(c(-111.891, 40.760)), crs = 4326), 3857)
area <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(st_buffer(centre, 6000)))

# Save the area in a square panel of `size` inches at `dpi`; `...` goes to
# geom_basemap(): a zoom or a symbol_scale.
panel <- function(file, ..., size = 2.4, dpi = 200) {
  p <- ggplot(area) +
    geom_basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", ..., attribution = FALSE) +
    geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = NA) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
  ggsave(file, p, width = size, height = size, dpi = dpi)
  last_rendering()  # what the plot drew at: $zoom, $symbol_scale, $dpi
}
dir <- tempdir()
```

```{r layout, include = FALSE}
# Lay out saved panels in a row of figures, each captioned with what was
# given and what the plot drew at. Not part of the lesson.
show_dir <- file.path(knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path"), "sharpness")
dir.create(show_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# The middle third of a PNG, to show its pixels.
crop_middle <- function(from, to) {
  a <- png::readPNG(from)
  h <- dim(a)[1]; w <- dim(a)[2]
  rows <- seq(floor(h / 3) + 1, floor(2 * h / 3))
  cols <- seq(floor(w / 3) + 1, floor(2 * w / 3))
  png::writePNG(a[rows, cols, , drop = FALSE], to)
}

chip <- function(text, hot = FALSE) sprintf('<span class="bm-chip%s">%s</span>', if (hot) " hot" else "", text)

# `cells`: a list of list(file, given, r, hot, width, alt); `hot` names the
# chip that changed ("zoom", "symbol" or "px"); `width` the image's width as
# a share of the cell.
knob_row <- function(cells, crop = FALSE) {
  html <- vapply(cells, function(cell) {
    name <- basename(cell$file)
    if (crop) crop_middle(cell$file, file.path(show_dir, name))
    else file.copy(cell$file, show_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
    r <- cell$r
    hot <- if (is.null(cell$hot)) "" else cell$hot
    chips <- paste(
      chip(sprintf("zoom %.2f", r$zoom), hot == "zoom"),
      chip(sprintf("symbol scale %.2f", r$symbol_scale), hot == "symbol"),
      chip(sprintf("%d &times; %d px", r$width, r$height), hot == "px")
    )
    style <- if (is.null(cell$width)) "" else sprintf(' style="width:%.0f%%"', 100 * cell$width)
    sprintf('<figure class="bm-knob"><img src="%s/%s" alt="%s"%s%s><figcaption><code>%s</code><span class="bm-chips">%s</span></figcaption></figure>',
            show_dir, name, cell$alt, if (crop) ' class="bm-pixels"' else "", style, cell$given, chips)
  }, character(1))
  cat('<div class="bm-knobs">', paste(html, collapse = "\n"), "</div>", sep = "\n")
}
```

## The device's dpi: the same map, only sharper

The same 2.4 inch panel saved at 96, 200 and 300 dpi. Shown is the middle
0.8 inch of each, enlarged so you can see the pixels. The zoom and the
label size don't move.

```{r}
row_dpi <- lapply(c(96, 200, 300), function(d) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("dpi-%d.png", d))
  list(file = file, given = sprintf("ggsave(dpi = %d)", d), r = panel(file, dpi = d), hot = "px")
})
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_along(row_dpi)) row_dpi[[i]]$alt <- sprintf(
  "The middle of the Salt Lake City panel saved at %s, enlarged: the same streets and labels, %s",
  row_dpi[[i]]$given, c("blocky at 96 dpi", "smoother at 200 dpi", "smoothest at 300 dpi")[i])
knob_row(row_dpi, crop = TRUE)
```

## `symbol_scale`: you set the label size, the zoom follows

Half the designed size, the designed size, and twice it. Halving the labels
frees room for one more zoom level of streets; doubling them takes one
away. Saved at 200 dpi.

```{r}
row_symbol <- lapply(c(0.5, 1, 2), function(s) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("symbol-%s.png", s))
  list(file = file, given = sprintf("symbol_scale = %s", s), r = panel(file, symbol_scale = s), hot = "zoom")
})
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_along(row_symbol)) row_symbol[[i]]$alt <- sprintf(
  "Salt Lake City with %s: %s", row_symbol[[i]]$given,
  c("small labels and many streets", "the style's designed label size", "large labels and only the main roads")[i])
knob_row(row_symbol)
```

## `zoom`: you set the detail, the label size follows

Zoom 10, 12 and 14, two levels apart. More detail in the same panel means
everything has to be drawn smaller: at zoom 14, labels are a small fraction
of their designed size. Saved at 200 dpi.

```{r}
row_zoom <- lapply(c(10, 12, 14), function(z) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("zoom-%d.png", z))
  list(file = file, given = sprintf("zoom = %d", z), r = panel(file, zoom = z), hot = "symbol")
})
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_along(row_zoom)) row_zoom[[i]]$alt <- sprintf(
  "Salt Lake City with %s: %s", row_zoom[[i]]$given,
  c("large labels and only highways", "streets and neighbourhood names", "every street, with tiny labels")[i])
knob_row(row_zoom)
```

These two rows are the same dial. `symbol_scale = 0.5` drew at zoom
`r sprintf("%.2f", row_symbol[[1]]$r$zoom)`, and `zoom =
`r sprintf("%.2f", row_symbol[[1]]$r$zoom)`` draws the identical picture.
Giving both would set the dial twice, which is why it's an error.

## Changing the panel size

Where the two differ: the same area saved in panels of 1.4, 2.4 and 3.4
inches, shown at their relative sizes.

With `symbol_scale` held (here left at 1), labels keep their printed size
and the detail changes: a smaller panel has room for less.

```{r}
sizes <- c(1.4, 2.4, 3.4)
row_panel_symbol <- lapply(sizes, function(s) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("panel-symbol-%s.png", s))
  list(file = file, given = sprintf("ggsave(width = %s)", s), r = panel(file, size = s), hot = "zoom", width = s / max(sizes))
})
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_along(row_panel_symbol)) row_panel_symbol[[i]]$alt <- sprintf(
  "Salt Lake City in a %s inch panel at symbol scale 1: labels the same printed size, %s", sizes[i],
  c("with only the main roads", "with more streets", "with the most streets")[i])
knob_row(row_panel_symbol)
```

With `zoom` held, the picture stays the same and is resized, labels
included. `zoom_for()` gives the zoom that a 3.4 inch panel draws at symbol
scale 1, so the small panels are shrunken copies of the large one:

```{r}
z <- zoom_for(area, 3.4)
z
row_panel_zoom <- lapply(sizes, function(s) {
  file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("panel-zoom-%s.png", s))
  list(file = file, given = sprintf("ggsave(width = %s)", s), r = panel(file, zoom = z, size = s), hot = "symbol", width = s / max(sizes))
})
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_along(row_panel_zoom)) row_panel_zoom[[i]]$alt <- sprintf(
  "Salt Lake City in a %s inch panel at the same zoom: the same map, %s", sizes[i],
  c("shrunk, labels too", "a little smaller", "at full size")[i])
knob_row(row_panel_zoom)
```

<p class="bm-credit">Map data: `r get_attribution(basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty"))`</p>

## Choosing

| I want | Set | What else changes |
|---|---|---|
| A sharper image of the same map | the device's dpi: `ggsave(dpi = 300)` | nothing |
| Bigger or smaller lines and labels | `symbol_scale` | the detail: a smaller symbol scale shows more roads and labels (a higher zoom), a larger one fewer |
| Exactly this level of detail | `zoom` | the size of lines and labels follows the panel size |
| The same map on a page and in a thumbnail | the same `zoom` for both, e.g. `zoom_for(bbox, 3.6, symbol_scale = 0.84)` | the thumbnail is the page map shrunk, labels too |
| Labels the same printed size on maps of different sizes | the same `symbol_scale` for all | each map gets the zoom that fits its panel |
| To know what a plot drew at | `last_rendering()` after drawing | nothing: it reads `$zoom`, `$symbol_scale`, `$dpi` |

`symbol_scale = 1` draws the style at its designed sizes, with a CSS pixel
1/96 inch on the page: a label the style sizes at 12 px prints at 9 pt.
`0.84` prints it at 84% of that. To keep the look of 0.3's
`geom_basemap(dpi = d)` saved with `ggsave(dpi = D)`, use
`symbol_scale = d / D`.

## Outside a plot

The same rule holds for `basemap()` on its own, where you give what a plot
would: any three of the extent, the zoom, the printed size and the symbol
scale give the fourth, and `dpi` only turns the printed size into pixels.
A size in inches (`units = "in"`) is the printed size, so a higher dpi is
the same map with more pixels:

```{r}
m <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = area, width = 2.4, height = 2.4, units = "in")
r96 <- render(m, dpi = 96)
r300 <- render(m, dpi = 300)
c(r96$zoom, r300$zoom)
c(r96$width, r300$width)
```

A size in pixels prints at pixels ÷ dpi inches, so there a higher dpi with
the same pixels prints the map smaller: with the extent fixed, at a lower
zoom:

```{r}
m <- basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", bounds = area, width = 480, height = 480)
c(render(m, dpi = 96)$zoom, render(m, dpi = 192)$zoom)
```

Python's `basemap()` and Rust's `Basemap` take the same settings; the rules
are in the [API reference](https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper/blob/main/docs/api.md).
